claims.explanation: Levocetirizine is a selective HRH1 antagonist, and its antiproliferative/cytotoxic effects in this screen most plausibly reflect HRH1 expression on tumor cells, since histamine signaling through H1 receptors can promote proliferation and survival in several cancers. The pattern of selective killing is therefore best explained by high HRH1 expression (sensitizing) and low HRH1 expression (protective), with TP53 loss and RAS/BRAF pathway activation as secondary modifiers that may lower the apoptotic threshold or enhance dependence on histamine-driven survival signals.

features.basis: drug target; H1 receptor mediates histamine-driven proliferation/survival in cancer cells
TP53 mutations are enriched in selectively killed lines, suggesting loss of apoptosis impairs recovery from drug stress
KRAS mutations appear in several killed lines and may increase dependence on histamine-linked survival signaling
BRAF mutations are common in killed melanoma/colorectal lines, possibly linking MAPK-driven proliferation to H1 signaling
PIK3CA mutations appear in multiple killed lines, suggesting PI3K pathway activation may enhance sensitivity
PTEN loss in killed lines may increase PI3K/AKT survival signaling that is disrupted by H1 blockade
CDKN2A loss in killed lines may impair cell-cycle arrest and increase drug sensitivity
NF1 mutations in killed lines may activate RAS/MAPK signaling and increase dependence on survival pathways
ATM mutations in killed lines may impair DNA damage responses and reduce recovery
ARID1A mutations appear in killed lines and may alter chromatin-dependent survival programs
KMT2D mutations are frequent in killed lines, possibly reflecting epigenetic vulnerability
